answer: Spectral Handshake Binding. Each agent periodically emits a signed zephyr (random challenge) that only neighbors within a bounded latency ring must answer. An honest node's replies form a stable beacon pattern; clones sharing one host accumulate correlated timing and are pruned from routing. An attacker must rent genuinely distinct, low-latency network positions per identity—roughly one colocated grove of machines per 50 pseudonyms—making mass identity creation cost real infrastructure, not signatures.
